title: 3rd Shift - Manufacturing Engineer - Engine Assembly
location: Lynn, Massachusetts, United States of America
description:
Job Description Summary
As Engine Assembly Manufacturing Engineer, you will provide on-shift manufacturing engineering support for engine assembly operations during 3rd shift, helping production teams safely build engines to quality, delivery, and cost targets. You will work directly with assemblers, technicians, quality, and support teams to resolve shop-floor issues, maintain process control, troubleshoot technical and hardware-related problems, and ensure work is performed to engineering and process requirements. You will support ongoing production by responding to disruptions, clarifying technical instructions, interpreting drawings and specifications, and making decisions within established procedures to keep assembly flowing.

This role is responsible for monitoring assembly processes, identifying and preventing defects or escapes, supporting root cause investigation and corrective actions, and driving practical process improvements that improve safety, quality, and productivity. The engineer must be able to balance immediate production needs with longer-term process discipline, communicate clearly across functions, and escalate issues that fall outside standard limits. On 3rd shift, this often means serving as a key technical resource for the operation with greater independence and ownership in real-time problem solving.

Job Description

Shift / Schedule Expectations

- This position supports 3rd shift operations
- Typical hours are 10:30 pm-7:30 am
- Regular onsite support is required during assigned shift
- May require overtime, weekend support, or schedule flexibility based on production needs
- Requires effective communication with 1st and 2nd shift teams to support shift handoff and issue continuity

Roles and Responsibilities

- Provide daily manufacturing engineering support for engine assembly operations on 3rd shift
- Support assembly processes by resolving technical issues, process constraints, tooling issues, nonconformances, and build interruptions
- Work directly with assembly technicians and operators on the shop floor to troubleshoot problems and implement practical solutions
- Interpret and apply engineering drawings, specifications, work instructions, process sheets, torque requirements, fits/clearances, and assembly sequencing requirements
- Develop, revise, and improve manufacturing processes, standard work, tooling, and production documentation
- Drive improvements in safety, quality, delivery, and cost
- Lead or support root cause investigations, corrective actions, and escape prevention related to assembly defects or process variation
- Partner with quality and operations to ensure compliance with engine assembly requirements, inspection requirements, and controlled process standards
- Support implementation of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives such as waste reduction, cycle time improvement, process simplification, and error-proofing
- Evaluate manufacturability and process risks and escalate issues when product or process integrity may be impacted
- Support new product introduction, process changes, tool changes, and production readiness activities as needed
- Communicate clearly across shifts and functions to ensure continuity of operations and effective issue resolution
- Use sound judgment to make timely decisions within established engineering and quality requirements, while escalating higher-risk issues appropriately

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Manufacturing, Mechanical, Aerospace, or related technical field (OR High school diploma / GED with at least 4 years of relevant experience in manufacturing, mechanical assembly, aircraft maintenance, engine assembly, engine overhaul/repair, aerospace production, or other closely related technical field)

Desired Characteristics

- Strong working knowledge of:
- Blueprint reading and engineering drawing interpretation
- GD&T
- Tooling, fixtures, torque tools, precision measurement, and mechanical assembly methods
- Process control and configuration control
- Root cause problem solving and corrective action
- Quality requirements, defect prevention, and escape prevention
- Standard work and lean manufacturing principles

- Experience with nonconformance disposition support, inspection findings, rework processes, and deviation management
- Familiarity with manufacturing documentation, routers, work instructions, process sheets, and revision-controlled technical data
- Experience collaborating with shop operations, quality, and design engineering to resolve build issues
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced production environment and make decisions with urgency and discipline
- Strong communication skills and ability to work respectfully with technicians, mechanics, and cross-functional teams

- Hands-on, practical mindset with strong shop-floor engagement
- Able to connect engineering requirements to real-world assembly execution
- Strong mechanical aptitude and product knowledge
- Effective at troubleshooting and resolving problems under production pressure
- Respectful, collaborative, and willing to learn from experienced technicians and operators
- Clear communicator who shares information across teams and shifts
- Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on safety, quality, and delivery
- High integrity, sound judgment, and disciplined decision-making in a regulated aerospace environment

The base pay range for this position is $92,000-$105,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 1, 2026.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Dowty, a GE Aerospace company is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for a wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft.

Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De Havilland Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J.

Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976, and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers.

In addition to technical development, we are also committed to supporting your broader personal development. Throughout your time on the course, you will be given the opportunity to participate in projects and training outside of your apprenticeships with the aim of enhancing both your interpersonal and intrapersonal skills.

Length of Program: 3 years plus End Point Assessment. You will receive a Level 3 Engineering and Manufacturing support technician qualification. The first year is full time at college with GET Engineering Training. In the second year you will be at college one day per week, with the remainder spent in the workplace. Third year is fulltime in the workplace, with time allocated for you to complete your EPA and any other required assignments.

As you progress through the years you will become a more integrated member of the team, taking on more responsibilities in your department and within the apprenticeship community.

Apprentices who have been through this program have successfully secured other roles, such as a Manufacturing Engineer.

Job Description Summary
GE Aerospace is seeking an experienced Advanced Staff Engineer – Power Electronics to provide technical leadership for advanced electrical power-conversion technologies and products. This role will lead complex engineering efforts supporting aerospace power generation, conversion, control, and energy-storage applications.

The successful candidate will combine deep power-electronics expertise with strong program execution, customer engagement, and cross-functional leadership skills. They will help shape technology roadmaps, develop innovative solutions, and guide technical teams through product and technology development.

Job Description

The Advanced Staff Engineer – Power Electronics will lead the design, analysis, development, and technical maturation of high-performance power-electronics systems. This includes power generation, power conversion, power-system analysis and controls, and energy-storage system integration.

Working across engineering, manufacturing, suppliers, customers, and other GE Aerospace organizations, this individual will provide technical direction, resolve complex program challenges, lead technical reviews, and ensure project requirements are met. The role requires strong expertise in power-conversion architectures, high-voltage/high-power hardware, controls, simulation, testing, and aerospace or military electrical standards.

Key Responsibilities

- Provide technical leadership to cross-functional teams supporting power-electronics technology and product-development programs.
- Lead the design and development of power-conversion systems, including power generation, power conversion, power-system controls, and energy-storage integration.
- Develop detailed technical analyses and present findings, design decisions, risks, and recommendations during technical reviews.
- Serve as the customer-facing technical lead or Principal Investigator for assigned technology and development programs.
- Coordinate technology-development efforts with other GE Aerospace teams and ensure work aligns with long-term product and technology roadmaps.
- Develop and execute plans to meet technical program requirements, schedules, quality objectives, and customer commitments.
- Partner with suppliers, manufacturing, systems engineering, and other technical disciplines to deliver robust and producible solutions.
- Identify technical risks and issues, develop corrective-action plans, and drive resolution through closure.
- Support customer proposals by reviewing requirements, assessing technical feasibility, and identifying capability gaps.
- Maintain awareness of power-electronics technology trends, competitive products, and market differentiators.
- Mentor and coach engineers, including developing technical talent for Principal Investigator and engineering-lead roles.
- Support leadership with technical reviews of customer requirements and product capabilities.

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related engineering discipline from an accredited university or college.
- Minimum of 10 years of experience in power electronics engineering.
- Demonstrated experience designing, analyzing, developing, or supporting power-conversion hardware and systems.
- Experience leading technical workstreams, engineering projects, or cross-functional technical teams.
- Ability to communicate technical information clearly to engineering teams, leadership, suppliers, and customers.
- Must qualify as a U.S. person under applicable export-control regulations, including U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and other protected individuals. Proof of status will be required before employment.

Desired Qualifications

- Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering.
- Experience with high-voltage, high-power converters or inverters, including systems of at least 10 kW and operating voltages above 270 V.
- Strong knowledge of DC-DC, DC-AC, and AC-DC power-conversion topologies and associated control methods.
- Experience with single-phase and three-phase electrical machines, including induction and synchronous machines in both motoring and generating modes.
- Knowledge of electromagnetic interference (EMI), including common-mode and differential-mode noise, and compliance with DO-160G and MIL-STD-461 requirements.
- Experience with transformer design, semiconductor switches, gate-driver design, PWM techniques, and power-stage layout.
- Experience with semiconductor loss modeling and validation testing, including double-pulse and pump-back testing.
- Familiarity with DSP-, microcontroller-, and FPGA-based control systems.
- Experience with circuit design and layout tools, such as Altium.
- Experience using simulation tools such as PLECS, LTspice, Simplorer, ANSYS/Ansoft, FEMM, MATLAB, or Simulink.
- Strong electrical circuit design, PCB layout, and hands-on laboratory testing experience.
- Experience supporting New Technology Introduction (NTI) and New Product Introduction (NPI) programs in power conversion.
- Strong influence, facilitation, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
- U.S. citizenship is preferred.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a senior-level power-electronics engineer who can lead both the technical solution and the people executing it. They have deep experience with high-voltage and high-power conversion hardware, understand power-system controls and electrical-machine interfaces, and can move confidently between simulation, design review, lab validation, manufacturing support, and customer discussions.

They are comfortable owning difficult technical problems, guiding engineering teams through trade studies and design decisions, and translating customer needs into practical, reliable product solutions. About GE Aerospace:

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Working at our Beavercreek Site

Our Beavercreek facility on Research Blvd. manufactures gas turbine tubes, ducts, and manifolds, and also has complex machining, fabrication and investment casting capabilities. Product engineering, new product development and testing is performed on site. This facility also does repair and overhaul of tubes, ducts, and manifolds. Our location on Heller drive manufactures turbine airfoils and has a focus on next generation technology. We have been awarded OSHAS’s highest safety rating.

Role Overview – Inspector

This role is responsible for performing preliminary, in‑process, and final inspections on aerospace components in accordance with new engine manuals and FAA‑approved technical data. You will play a key role in ensuring airworthiness, quality, and on‑time delivery for critical engine components.

In this role, you will:

- Execute all manufacturing work with a rigorous focus on safety, quality, and the critical nature of aircraft parts.
- Perform preliminary, in‑process, and final inspections on engine and component parts
- Inspect parts for defects, dimensional accuracy, and compliance to engineering specifications and customer requirements
- You will heavily utilize a computer to navigate through different programs, blueprints, software, and Microsoft products
- Use hands and fingers to move parts, use measurement instruments, and manually examine parts
- Read and interpret OEM manuals, blueprints, and, where applicable, FAA‑approved technical data

- You show up reliably, your team counts on you
- You’re willing to learn multiple roles to support the team

- Prior experience in an aerospace or regulated environment with strong focus on documentation, traceability, and compliance

- Demonstrated pride in workmanship and commitment to quality
- Strong attendance and punctuality record, with availability to work overtime as needed

Job Description Summary

Job Description

Aerospace Tig Welder

About GE Aerospace:

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Working at our Beavercreek Site

GE Aerospace operations have been part of the Beavercreek community for over 75 years! Our Beavercreek facility on Research Blvd. manufactures gas turbine tubes, ducts, and manifolds, and also has complex machining, fabrication and investment casting capabilities. Product engineering, new product development and testing is performed on site. This facility also does repair and overhaul of tubes, ducts, and manifolds. Our location on Heller drive manufactures turbine airfoils and has a focus on next generation technology. We have been awarded OSHAS’s highest safety rating.

Role Overview – TIG Welder

In this role, you will:

- Execute all manufacturing work with a rigorous focus on safety, quality, and the critical nature of aircraft parts
- Weld metal components as specified by layouts, blueprints, diagrams, or manufacturing operations sheets (MOS), using TIG welding equipment
- Set up and connect cables from the welding unit to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse as specified
- Manually guide torch along weld lines, maintaining arc length and travel speed to achieve the required fusion and bead, using visual and audible cues from the weld
- Weld in flat, horizontal, vertical, and overhead positions
- Examine welds to confirm bead size and conformance to specifications
- Manually apply filler rod, clean weld joints and workpieces, and prepare rework parts for welding
- Position or clamp workpieces together, or assemble them in jigs/fixtures; may tack assemblies together
- Use a computer daily to check email and view/download shop drawings and work instructions
- Cross‑train to work in all areas of the team and run other processes as production needs require
- Train other team members on standard work and machine operation as needed
- Assist in other areas as needed and directed by People Leader

The Ideal Candidate

- You show up reliably, your team counts on you
- You’re willing to learn multiple roles to support the team

- Execute all manufacturing work with a rigorous focus on safety, quality, and the critical nature of aircraft parts.
- Follow all safety rules when using and maintaining shop equipment; pass and maintain required vision testing
- Use basic and shop math (fractions, decimals, whole numbers) to support accurate, precise work
- Read and apply technical information and blueprints to produce high‑quality parts
- Use standard measuring tools (manual calipers, micrometers) to verify dimensions and prevent defects
- Follow written, verbal, and visual instructions to complete work on time and support on‑time delivery
- Use tools and materials responsibly, help reduce scrap and rework, and raise issues early to support continuous improvement in safety, quality, and delivery (SQD)

Required Qualifications

- High school diploma or GED
- Successful completion of a TIG welding training course (formal program), or previous TIG welding experience (minimum 6 months)
- Successful completion of the Unison‑Dayton TIG Welding Assessment
- This role may encounter high risk or hazardous operations and/or include working shifts beyond a standard workweek. As such, a requirement of the role is to be at least 18 years of age by the time of joining.

Preferred Qualifications

- Team‑oriented, professional approach to working with peers and leaders
- Demonstrated pride in workmanship and commitment to quality
- Strong attendance and punctuality record, with availability to work overtime as needed
- Ability to make decisions based on approved work instructions, experience, and available data
- Drive to meet or exceed job requirements and performance expectations
- Ability to work effectively under general supervision, including performing routine assignments independently
- Ability to carry out operations according to set procedures or sequences
- Willingness to receive and act on constructive feedback

Additional Information

- Wages: $24.10 – $30.00 per hour based on experience
- Additional 10%/hour premium for 2nd or 3rd shift
- Ability to lift up to 40 pounds; may occasionally lift up to 50 pounds (with assistance)
- Strong safety focus with daily and monthly reviews; site has been awarded OSHA’s highest safety rating
- Most protective gear provided, including hearing protection as needed; GE Aerospace provides a $125 voucher for safety shoes and a voucher for prescription safety glasses if needed
- Work in and around moving equipment such as stand‑up forklifts, mobile carts, and cranes; normal machining operations may generate dust, fumes, or smoke (not over OSHA permissible exposure levels)
- Team‑oriented environment with opportunities to share ideas and make recommendations with peers and leadership
- Work may involve standing in one place for extended periods, walking, and climbing stairs; most areas are climate‑controlled

Our Culture

We strive to keep a safe, high‑performing, and enjoyable shop atmosphere while maintaining the highest level of quality output. We work together to make the “impossible” happen and are looking for people like you to join us. If you’re a team‑oriented welder who takes pride in your work, shares ideas, and wants to grow your skills, we’d like to meet you.

- Based on daily list driven by finance and variance count cycles, reels and trays must be retrieved from its location, brought to the x-ray counter, count the material, and update the count on a physical sheet and turn into Noel for count/inventory validation.

Job Description Summary
Transform engine and spare-part delivery for Defense Engines & Services (DES). This role owns the product vision, roadmap, and end-to-end lifecycle for the data, analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI) capability that makes that transformation possible. Act as the customer representative for a portfolio of interdependent products spanning new engine production and Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO), from demand and forecast through fulfillment and service and support. Success is measured through DES KPIs, led by on-time delivery and spare-part output, then inventory and net productivity.

This is a forward-deployed role. You will work alongside the planners, operators, and engineers who own the delivery, and you will build digital capability with them, taking AI-enabled ideas from concept to medium and high-fidelity working prototypes on real production data.

Job Description

This role will also require in-person attendance for New Hire Orientation on Day 1

Roles and Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

- Own all aspects of the lifecycle (planning, forecasting, production) for multiple interdependent data, analytics, and AI products that together form the DES delivery transformation program and represent the customer in every scope and sequencing tradeoff.

- Build and maintain the DES data and analytics product roadmap, sequence it against the constraints that actually limit engine and spare-part output, and identify and secure the stakeholders needed to support it.

- Stand up self-service data and analytics on manufacturing, quality, and delivery data so planners, buyers, and shop leaders answer their own questions in the moment rather than opening a DT ticket. This closes the single largest capability gap in the portfolio.

- Operationalize and sustain value from advanced analytics and agentic AI investments, and move proven prototypes inside the operating model rather than leaving them adjacent to it, where they stay advisory.

- Partner with central DT and Enterprise Data on data fabric and ontology adoption so DES manufacturing, quality, and delivery data is modeled once and reused across products.

- Take AI-enabled ideas from concept to working software. Build low-fidelity proofs to test feasibility, then advance the survivors to medium and high-fidelity prototypes on real production data, in the hands of real users, and decide quickly which ones earn production investment and which get killed.

- Work forward-deployed. Embed with operators, planners, and engineers at the Genba, build with them rather than collecting requirements and handing them off, and stay on the problem until the capability is in use.

- Use rapid prototyping as a countermeasure inside Daily Management, converting Key Performance Indicator (KPI) and Targets to Improve (TTI) gaps into working capability in weeks rather than quarters.

- Define the value case in delivery terms up front (engine days, turnaround time, schedule adherence, inventory turns, cost), drive early materialization of benefits, and report outcomes against the 2026 DES measures. Stop or redirect work that does not move a delivery number.

- Influence Executive Band (EB) leaders and below on investment decisions, and partner with business, finance, and DT leadership to align Digital Technology spend with value stream priorities.

- Set data and AI standards across the DES horizontal so use, implementation, support, and technical integrity stay consistent and do not fragment by product line.

- Operate as a player-coach. Mentor product managers and engineers on systems thinking for large-scale problems, lean and experimental product practice, and raise the team's data and AI fluency.

- Manage supplier and contractor partners delivering analytics and AI work, hold them to outcomes, and reduce the team's dependence on expensive external delivery.

- Lead risk management for the portfolio, including export control, cybersecurity, data governance, and responsible AI, and design controls into products instead of relying on exception processes.

Business Acumen

- Translates business problems into product bets, quantifies the value, and makes tradeoffs across a multi-product portfolio based on business priority rather than the loudest request.

- Establishes performance metrics and drives continuous improvement across systems, processes, and resources.

- Demonstrated customer focus; evaluates decisions through the eyes of the operator on the floor and partners with the business to shape future initiatives.

- Decomposes problems and decides when the problem or the solution is not fully defined.

- Constructs multiyear scenarios for data-centric methods and technologies under uncertainty, and interprets industry trends that should inform the roadmap.

Leadership

- Sets and changes direction at the enterprise level by building direct and indirect support for ideas, largely without formal authority.

- Leads and influences across a complex matrix organization, including Executive Band leaders and their teams, and incorporates stakeholder input while still deciding.

- Directs and mentors others toward a systems thinking approach for solving large-scale problems, and removes roadblocks on behalf of the team.

- Owns decisions, including outcomes and any required rework plans.

- Acts as a catalyst for change, rewards early adopters, and builds a culture of proactive problem solving rather than reactive break-fix.

Personal Attributes

- Excellent written and oral communication; presents concise facts and the implications of alternatives in a way that is relevant to senior leadership and customers.
- Strategic thinker who converts vision into a concrete action plan with named owners and dates.

- Manages uncertainty for self and others, and makes confident decisions when problems or solutions are not 100% defined.

- Curious and creative; removes barriers to the creativity of others and pushes simplicity and speed.

- Biased toward demonstration over documentation. Would rather show a working prototype than present a plan for one.

- Strong analytical, project management, and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize under pressure and tight deadlines.

Required Qualification

Bachelor’s degree from accredited university or college with minimum of 10 years of professional experience OR Associates degree with minimum of 13 years of professional experience OR High School Diploma with minimum of 15 years of professional experience

Minimum 8 years of professional experience in IT

Note: Military experience is equivalent to professional experience

Ability to travel; 10-50%

Eligibility Requirement:

-Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job.

Desired Qualification

Technical Expertise

- Hands-on builder with a forward-deployed engineering mindset. Personally produces working artifacts (data pipelines, ontology and semantic models, notebooks, agent workflows, and functional user interfaces) rather than only specifying them, and is fluent in Python, SQL, or equivalent.

- Demonstrated ability to move an idea across fidelity levels under time pressure: proof of concept to prove feasibility, medium fidelity to prove the workflow, high fidelity to prove production readiness and earn investment.

- Demonstrated ownership of data platform and advanced analytics products at scale, covering ingestion, modeling, governance, performance, and self-service consumption.

- Working fluency with modern analytics and AI, including machine learning, large language model, retrieval, and agentic patterns, and the judgment to know where those methods do not belong.

- Working knowledge of manufacturing and MRO data and systems, including Manufacturing Execution System (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), quality, and shop-floor technology, and how that data becomes a delivery or inventory decision.

- Deep technology, process, and domain expertise sufficient to influence product design whether the product is built internally or bought.

- Strong track record of understanding current and emerging technologies, demonstrated through training, job experience, or industry activities.

- Demonstrated understanding of Lean Six Sigma principles (for example, Green Belt certified) and comfort operating inside a Daily Management system.

Dowty, a GE Aerospace company is based in Gloucestershire. Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De Havilland Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J.

The primary purpose of the role is to undertake an apprenticeship 4yr program to achieve Calibration Technician status at Dowty.

description:
Job Description Summary
At GE Aerospace, we are advancing the future of flight through a relentless focus on Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost and through FLIGHT DECK, our proprietary operating system that develops and empowers our people.. The EHS Engineer plays a critical role in supporting a safe, compliant, and operationally effective work environment across manufacturing, engineering, test, and site support functions.
This role partners closely with operations, maintenance, engineering, and leadership teams to identify and reduce risk, ensure compliance with environmental, health, and safety requirements, and drive continuous improvement. The role is expected to apply FLIGHT DECK principles by helping teams establish standard work, use daily and visual management to expose gaps, and drive disciplined problem solving and action planning to improve site performance.
The ideal candidate brings strong technical knowledge, practical problem-solving capability, and the ability to influence teams at all levels while demonstrating the GE Aerospace behaviors of Respect for People, Continuous Improvement, and Customer Driven, always with unyielding integrity.

Job Description

Company Overview:

Are you ready to see your career take flight? At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. We are a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen.

Site Overview:

For more than 40 years, our advanced facilities in Singapore have led aerospace innovation across the Asia Pacific region. From automating processes to leveraging smart factory technologies, robotics, and additive manufacturing, GE Aerospace is shaping the future of aviation. Responsible for more than 60% of our global repair volume, our Singapore site is the largest site for engine component maintenance, repair and overhaul work. We can’t do this work without talented people like you.

Join us and be part of our journey to innovate and excel in the aerospace industry.

Role Overview:

- Support and lead site environmental, health, and safety programs in alignment with business, regulatory, and customer requirements

- Partner with manufacturing, engineering, maintenance, and support teams to identify hazards and implement effective risk reduction actions

- Establish, improve, and sustain standard work for key EHS processes, recognizing that standard work documents and visualizes the best-known way to complete a task or process today and forms the foundation for continuous improvement and sustainment.

- Conduct and support risk assessments, job hazard analyses, ergonomic evaluations, audits, inspections, and compliance reviews

- Investigate incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions; lead or facilitate root cause analysis, structured problem solving, and corrective action development to close gaps in performance and drive impact to SQDC..

- Drive timely closure of corrective and preventive actions and verify effectiveness of implemented controls

- Use daily and visual management practices to help teams visualize targets and results, track progress to goals, problem solve when off plan, and review process effectiveness.

- Support visual management and action follow-up using standard FLIGHT DECK components including:

- Performance measures tied to SQDIP

- Gap analysis using TAGS (trend, actual, gap, standard)

- Actions and escalations with specific action, owner, expected completion date, expected impact, and current status.

- Monitor site EHS performance metrics, identify trends, and communicate results, risks, and priorities to site leadership

- Support compliance with applicable federal, state, local, permit, and company EHS requirements

- Assist with management of environmental programs including, as applicable, hazardous waste, air emissions, wastewater, stormwater, chemical management, and required reporting

- Support implementation and sustainment of programs such as lockout/tagout, machine guarding, PPE, fall protection, confined space, contractor safety, ergonomics, and hazard communication

- Deliver, coordinate, or support EHS training for employees, leaders, and contractors

- Participate in emergency preparedness planning, drills, and response coordination

- Partner with frontline teams and leaders at genba to proactively expose problems, remove barriers, and support real-time problem solving to meet customer expectations.

- Contribute to kaizen activity and continuous improvement efforts that improve EHS performance, operational stability, and employee engagement.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college in Engineering, Environmental Science, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, or related field

- At least 5 years of experience in environmental, health, and safety, manufacturing, industrial operations, or related technical field

- Registered with the Ministry of Manpower as a Workplace Safety and Health Officer (WSHO) and SCDF Fire Safety Manager (FSM).

- Strong knowledge of Singapore’s WSH legislation and compliance requirements

- Experience with incident investigation, structured problem solving, and corrective action management

- Ability to work in a team-based environment where performance is measured and actions are managed through regular operating cadences and visual management

- Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work across functions and organizational levels

- Demonstrated ability to analyze issues, prioritize actions, and drive execution in an operational environment

Preferred Qualifications

- Strong commitment to safety, compliance, and respect for people

- Action-oriented with a practical and disciplined approach to execution

- Effective facilitator of cross-functional problem solving and kaizen

- Comfortable working both strategically and tactically

- Strong data analysis, organization, and follow-through skills

- Clear communicator with the ability to engage hourly employees, technical teams, and site leadership

- Demonstrated mindset of continuous improvement

- Willingness to expose problems, engage associates, drive accountability, ask questions, check for understanding, and lead from the front

- Ability to create urgency around closing gaps and sustaining improvements through standardization and follow-up

description:
Job Description Summary
GE Aerospace is seeking a skilled, hands-on Engineering Test Technician to join our engineering laboratory team in Grand Rapids, Michigan. This role supports the testing, troubleshooting, repair, and validation of aerospace electronic products and test equipment. You will work closely with design engineering teams to resolve hardware issues, verify performance against drawings and specifications, and help ensure reliable, high-quality products for aerospace applications.

Job Description

The Engineering Test Technician will perform product testing and debug at both the complete-unit (“black box”) and circuit card assembly (CCA) levels. This individual will troubleshoot analog, digital, and microprocessor-based circuits; build, repair, and maintain test equipment; and support test-station setup and calibration.

This is a highly hands-on engineering lab role requiring strong electronics troubleshooting, soldering, component-level repair, and test-equipment experience. The successful candidate can work independently, document findings clearly, and collaborate effectively with design engineering and cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities

- Perform functional, diagnostic, and verification testing on electronic products, CCAs, and complete units against engineering drawings, specifications, and test procedures.
- Troubleshoot and debug analog, digital, and microprocessor-based circuits at the component, board, unit, and test-station levels.
- Perform soldering, desoldering, assembly, disassembly, modification, and repair of electronic hardware and test equipment; maintain applicable solder certification.
- Conduct component testing and evaluation on electrical devices while meeting defined schedule and budget requirements.
- Build, check out, set up, calibrate, and maintain test equipment, fixtures, and test stations.
- Partner with design engineers to identify root causes, resolve failures, validate corrective actions, and improve product quality.
- Use Windows-based tools and lower-level programming interfaces as needed; JTAG programming experience is beneficial.
- Support lab computer, network, and IT security setup activities as required.
- Document test results, failures, repairs, and technical findings accurately and clearly.
- Follow applicable safety, quality, compliance, and export-control requirements.

Basic Qualifications

- Associate degree in Electrical Engineering/Electronics Technology, an Electronic Technician certificate, or a high school diploma/GED with at least 5 years of related electronics testing experience or relevant military experience.
- 3-5 years of hands-on experience in an engineering lab, electronics test, product test, avionics, military electronics, or similar technical environment.
- Demonstrated experience testing and troubleshooting analog, digital, and microprocessor-based electronic circuits.

description:
Job Description Summary
Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) aims to reveal any hidden defects and a high need of reliability, by applying accelerated environment stresses, such as vibrations or thermal cycling, to a product, using various testing procedures to accomplish this. ESS testing helps to prepare products for their real-world applications, so the testing conditions will often be the most extreme which the product may face in the real world. ESS tests can expose component failures. Thermal testing may find faults related to seal and gasket failures, insufficient wiring insulation and other component-level defects.

Job Description

At GE Aerospace in Bohemia, you will be part of a collaborative and diverse team that values your unique perspectives and innovative spirit. You will have the opportunity to work smarter, not harder, through our ongoing LEAN transformation. Your contributions will have a meaningful impact on millions of lives, and you will share in our sense of purpose and pride. If you are ready to elevate your future, come aboard and help us advance aviation technologies for today and tomorrow.

- Career Growth: GE isn’t just a great place to start your career—it’s a great place to expand and grow your career. Many entry-level employees grow into leadership roles in operations or other parts of the business. There are also opportunities to continue your career at GE in Bohemia or across the globe.

- Benefits: Our range of benefits includes health care starting on day one, 401 (k) savings plan with generous employer match, paid time off and more

- Education Assistance: GE encourages employees to continue their education and provides financial support to further employee learning.

- Work environment: GE Aerospace facility located in Islip, Long Island is dedicated to the design and manufacture of power conversion & control products, Battery systems, Lighting Controllers, Frequency Converters, Digital Control Products, Control Panels, Inverters, Power supplies and Advanced power conversion applications.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Testing may be conducted on the part level, assembly level or unit level.

- Combined Temperature and Electrodynamic Vibration

- Rapid Transition Rates

- Profile Execution for Extended Test Durations

- “Shake and Bake”

- Altitude

- Thermal Vacuum (TVAC)

These tests are conducted in dedicated environmental test chambers with advanced testing equipment

- Technicians place the product on vibration table testing X,Y,Z axis. Vibratory testing is more likely to uncover loose hardware and connectors, insufficiently torqued screw assemblies and weaknesses in switches and circuit breakers.

- Technicians place the product in an environmental test chamber based on product profiles and monitors temperature change. Other stimuli are applied to find defects in the product being tested.

- Test the product recording all successful tests and record all failures for further troubleshooting using specification data and schematics.

- Performs basic tasks such as electro-mechanical set up, utilizing cables, connectors, and test equipment, must be able to adjust and modify machine profiles as need to meet specification.

- Run ATE (automatic test equipment) and STE (standard test equipment).

Job Description Summary
The Europe & Asia Transportation Planning & Execution Manager is responsible for translating global transportation strategy into executable regional transportation plans across Europe and Asia. This role develops routing plans, execution models, localized processes, and supplier-management routines that enable consistent, scalable transportation performance across sites, suppliers, carriers, and lanes. 1.

A key priority for this role is to plan the week and monitor the day to deliver CTL and CTB weekly objectives. The successful candidate will leverage AI, analytics, digital tools, and process automation to improve transportation quality, strengthen execution discipline, accelerate continuous improvement, and deliver measurable cost and productivity benefits. These additions align with the draft’s stated focus on performance management, continuous improvement, and turning strategy into repeatable execution capability

This is not primarily a shipment-tracking or expediting role. It operates one level above individual shipment execution and is accountable for building the routing, processes, supplier routines, and operating mechanisms that enable reliable transportation performance at scale.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities

- Develop and maintain transportation routing plans for Europe and Asia aligned with global transportation strategy, including mode selection, carrier assignments, gateway strategy, consolidation approach, cutoff requirements, transit-time expectations, contingency routing, and escalation requirements.
- Translate transportation strategy into executable lane, site, supplier, system, and process-level plans that can be consistently deployed across the region.
- Establish implementation plans for major transportation changes, including supplier readiness, site readiness, carrier onboarding, routing instructions, systems requirements, data requirements, communications, escalation paths, and performance monitoring.
- Translate global transportation standard work into practical regional processes while allowing appropriate localization for infrastructure, supplier capability, operating hours, regulatory requirements, and market conditions.
- Standardize successful processes across sites and suppliers and reduce unnecessary regional variation caused by legacy local practices.
- Serve as a primary regional interface with transportation suppliers across Europe and Asia, including freight forwarders, airlines, trucking providers, parcel/express carriers, and 4PL partners.
- Ensure suppliers understand and execute routing, service, data, escalation, and performance requirements; conduct operating reviews and drive corrective action when performance does not meet expectations.
- Lead implementation of transportation plans across GE Aerospace sites and suppliers throughout Europe and Asia, ensuring clarity on provider selection, shipment timing, routing, documentation, cutoffs, escalation procedures, data requirements, and compliance expectations.
- Support supplier launches, sourcing transitions, manufacturing transfers, new facilities, MRO expansions, distribution-network changes, and other major supply-chain initiatives.
- Lead the regional operating rhythm by planning the week and monitoring the day to deliver CTL and CTB weekly objectives, using daily visibility and exception management to identify gaps early and drive countermeasures.
- Monitor performance across transit time, routing compliance, carrier performance, lane reliability, premium freight, shipment exceptions, lead-time performance, supplier execution, data quality, capacity constraints, and recurring failure modes.
- Use AI, analytics, digital tools, and automation to improve decision making, transportation visibility, process discipline, data quality, continuous improvement, and cost performance.
- Identify and scale technology-enabled opportunities to reduce waste, improve quality, lower premium freight, and deliver measurable cost and productivity benefits.
- Drive structured problem solving and continuous improvement with sites, suppliers, carriers, and transportation partners.
- Partner closely with regional distribution capabilities, including Netherlands and Singapore spare-parts operations, to ensure integration into the global transportation network.

- Significant experience in transportation, logistics, supply chain, or related operations

- Experience working with carriers, freight forwarders, and/or 4PL providers
- Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into execution across lanes, suppliers, sites, systems, and processes, consistent with the draft’s ideal candidate profile
- Demonstrated ability to leverage AI, analytics, and digital tools to improve execution, quality, continuous improvement, and cost performance

Preferred Qualifications

- Strong knowledge of European and Asian air and road freight networks
- Experience managing transportation suppliers across complex regional networks
- Strong analytical and process-development capability
- Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders, sites, and suppliers without direct authority

Along with this you will be defining test specifications and supporting physical tests. Ultimately products you will work on will move into production and gain flight hours.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Engineering

Engineering is at the centre of what we do, and we are looking for talented, innovative engineers who can help us design and develop products for today, tomorrow, and in the future. If you are a dreamer, doer, and inventor who wants your voice to be heard and see your ideas take flight, this is the opportunity for you.

Roles and Responsibilities

In the 12-month Mechanical Engineering (Systems) Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience covering all aspects of engineering from requirements and design analysis to product design to defining test specifications.

During this placement, you may work (depend on the role) across the product development lifecycle, from new product introduction (NPI) to in-service support.

We have different types of roles in this area; here is a brief snapshot into each:

Mechanical Design & Analysis (Cheltenham) - This hardware placement sits within the mechanical design area and combines both mechanical design and analysis work, typically across several projects or 1–2 larger programmes. You will gain hands-on experience with CAD and associated design tools, as well as structural and thermal analysis tools, while supporting activities such as production support, fault finding, root cause investigation, and implementing permanent corrective actions. Depending on project maturity, you may be involved in early concept and design development or in validation and verification as products transition into production. The types of products you could work on include power distribution units, controllers, and display systems, providing broad exposure to the hardware product lifecycle.

Mechanical Engineering (Bristol) - contributing to the design, analysis, and testing of mechanical systems and components in an industrial environment. This role is aimed at candidates with a strong interest in mechanical design, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and materials science, who want to apply their engineering knowledge in practice. Key responsibilities include assisting with the design and development of mechanical systems, using computational tools such as ANSYS, SolidWorks, and MATLAB to analyse performance, and supporting testing and validation by helping to set up experiments and interpret test data. You will also contribute to research and development activities, exploring new technologies and materials for mechanical applications.

MTO Engineering - Robotic Automation Team (Bristol) - developing robotic and automated mechanical systems that improve inspection and repair within GE Aerospace’s MRO (Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul) network. As a Mechanical Engineering (Systems) Placement Student, you would join a multi-disciplinary Robotic Automation team, working across the full development lifecycle: defining problems and capturing requirements with project teams and customers, researching and integrating commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) solutions, collecting and processing data, and contributing to the design, rapid prototyping, testing, and industrialization of new inspection and repair systems. Key responsibilities include helping to define and develop automated/robotic processes, designing and testing in-house prototype solutions, and producing technical documentation such as specifications, installation procedures, and system configurations. The role is aimed at someone enthusiastic about innovative solutions that combine mechanical design, automation, robotics, and software integration.

You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK.

This opportunity is offered in our Bristol (Bristol Robotic Services) and Cheltenham sites, during the process we will ask you to share your location preferences.

GE Aerospace, Bristol Robotic Services (BRS) is a small tightknit office located in Bristol, South West England. We are a team of ~50 talented, dedicated and hardworking employees who collaborate to solve very interesting challenges in the aerospace industry. Every day at BRS is unique; you will be presented with exciting technical problems to solve and be given the space to innovate bespoke solutions. Given the small size of the company, it is very clear to see the impact your work makes, so if you are someone who grabs opportunity with both hands, you will find your time here very rewarding.

We are looking for high-energy, self-motivated individuals with the vision to help carry our business forward.  The work is academically rigorous, intellectually demanding, and requires exceptional problem-solving, communication, leadership and interpersonal skills. That being said, we are a very collaborative bunch so we don’t need you to be an expert in everything, we have experts here who will mentor and coach you into developing the skills you need.

Our offices are in Bristol in the South West of England – an area fast becoming a major centre for robotics. The South West is a beautiful place to live, with good infrastructure, great universities and fabulous beaches not far away from the city of Bristol. Our offices are located a few minutes’ walk from Filton Abbey Wood Station and on a regular bus route.

With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy.

Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge. Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come.

At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential.

Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight.

The role requires close collaboration with Programmes, Finance, Operations, and Logistics, including supporting cross-functional reviews and small improvement projects in reporting, data quality, and process flow. The placement offers end-to-end exposure to field service operations, practical experience in metrics, financial and logistics coordination, and development of professional communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.

The role requires adapting to different people and environments daily, understanding departmental challenges to set maintenance priorities, communicating with various stakeholders and responding to critical needs, and learning from experienced staff to improve existing processes and work-scopes. The role is designed to give the intern practical experience in managing internal special projects, supporting customer engagement, and becoming familiar with program management practices, procedures, internal systems, and standard work. The placement will work closely with stakeholders, customers, and colleagues across multiple functions, while contributing to business-focused projects, driving actions to closure, presenting findings and recommendations, and developing communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

- BizJet Portfolio (Cheltenham) - you will gain exposure to the complete program and product lifecycle, from new product introduction through to repair and overhaul services. The programs team you will join is a dynamic and growing portfolio, offering a strong opportunity to contribute to day‑to‑day program activities and develop core program management skills. Key activities include reviewing customer purchase orders and supporting the Program Team in managing the product orderbook, ensuring alignment between customer portals and internal order management systems. You will support sales and operational review meetings through orderbook management and engagement with key stakeholders involved in demand changes. You will help with obsolescence management by developing regular reviews with key functions, monitoring stock run‑out dates, and improving communication with other programs where obsolescence risk is shared. You will act as a “voice of the customer”, supporting communication between internal teams and the customer, engaging with customers to help secure invoice payment in support of cash targets, and helping to organise and support program review meetings with customers.

- OE Value Stream Programs (Dowty) - focuses on planning, coordinating, and delivering manufactured spare parts to ensure reliable aftermarket support. The role owns the integrated production and delivery plan for defined part families, aligning production and materials with customer demand and business priorities, and applying a structured operating model to meet Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost objectives. Working cross‑functionally with materials planning, manufacturing, quality, sourcing, logistics, and customer‑facing teams, the role manages production schedules, monitors performance, addresses risks and issues, and keeps customers informed through clear, proactive communication on delivery status, changes, and recovery plans. It combines operational planning, data‑driven performance management, and customer relationship management to improve delivery reliability and overall supply chain effectiveness.

- Programme Management Office (Cheltenham) - supporting the successful delivery of complex projects from early bid and concept stages through to closure. The PMO Project Controller is responsible for managing budgets and schedules using standardised tools, maintaining integrated project plans, and providing analysis to identify and mitigate cost and schedule risks. The role serves as a key point of contact for project management tools and practices, coaching project and technical leaders and performing earned value analysis to support informed decision-making. It also supports structured change and risk management processes, including preparing change documentation, participating in risk and opportunity reviews, and ensuring decisions are clearly recorded. In addition, the PMO Project Controller contributes to accurate project forecasting and helps coordinate resource plans across multiple teams to ensure projects are appropriately staffed and controlled.

The individual will be responsible for maintaining robust document control across NPI, production execution and aftermarket, coordinating actions with the integrated program team (IPT) following tollgate reviews and key meetings, and ensuring all program risks and opportunities are captured and managed in the digital thread tool. The role also includes monitoring and reporting touch labour and material performance against targets, identifying opportunities to eliminate non‑value‑added work using lean principles and project management principles. Through these activities, the individual will gain hands-on experience in quality assurance, QMS, risk management, and end-to-end program execution.

You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Role Overview

GE Aerospace is seeking a T700/CT7 (Turboshaft) Depot Subject Matter Expert - Shop Floor to support hands-on depot execution for T700/CT7 engines, modules, and components. This role is ideal for a practical engine maintenance professional who brings deep shop knowledge, strong technician instincts, and a commitment to safe, disciplined execution. This role is full time, on-site at customer facility located in Deblin, Poland.

· Support depot maintenance execution for T700-GE-701C/D, CT7-2E1 and CT7-8E engines, modules, and components across inspection, disassembly, assembly, repair support, and final preparation activities.

· Train the customer and support engine and module disassembly and assembly activities with focus on task discipline, cleanliness, hardware accountability, and safe execution.

· Work closely with GE internal and customer operations, quality, and engineering teams to maintain safe, efficient, and compliant maintenance flow.

· Demonstrated experience in T700/CT7 engine maintenance, depot operations, or closely related turboshaft engine shop activity.

· Demonstrated tooling discipline and ability to reinforce efficient, organized, and repeatable work practices.

The Information Security Manager (ISM) is the primary cybersecurity focal at the site. Company Overview:

GE Aerospace Engine Services Malaysia (GEESM) in Subang is a key part of our global maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) network, supporting the service of commercial aircraft engines, components, and accessories with world-class technical expertise. Established in 1997 as a Center of Excellence for CFM56 engines, the site has continued to grow, including becoming GE Aerospace’s first LEAP MRO facility outside the U.S. We are also expanding our footprint in Malaysia with a new LEAP engine MRO facility in Sepang! Employing more than 700 highly skilled local professionals and providing MRO services to more than 50 airlines worldwide, GEESM continues to exceed our customers’ expectations. With our technical expertise and pioneering spirit, we elevate the flying experience to new heights.

Role Overview:

Cybersecurity Implementation & Monitoring:

- Lead the Site Cyber Implementation Team to deploy and sustain the Cyber Playbook and other corporate cyber standards.

- Track site-level cyber activities and risks (e.g., CMMC/IA defects, EASA Part-IS, vulnerabilities, endpoint monitoring coverage) and maintain a site cyber action plan.

- Report cybersecurity metrics in Shop MOR/Daily Management and provide updates to site and DT leadership.

- Act as first-level approver for security-related change management requests (e.g., firewall rules, ports, OT/IT connectivity), ensuring changes are risk-assessed, documented, and compliant.

Auditing and Compliance:

- Ensure the site complies with applicable cybersecurity regulations, standards, and contractual requirements (global, regional, and customer-specific).

- Partner with relevant functions to support customer audits, regulatory inspections, and technical reviews.

- Assist with root cause analysis, corrective actions, and clarifications during and after external and internal audits.

- Support incident response readiness, including communication of roles, escalation paths, and participation in drills.

- Contribute to post-incident reviews and drive implementation of corrective and preventive actions.

Cybersecurity Culture and Continuous Improvement:

- Actively promote cybersecurity rules and best practices within the facility.

- Conduct presentations and training sessions for various departments to enhance cybersecurity awareness and ownership.

- Use appropriate communication channels to disseminate cybersecurity information and expectations.

- Engage with shop floor, OT, and cross-functional stakeholders (Operations, Quality, EHS, Compliance, Facilities, BISOs, DT) to embed cybersecurity into daily operations and projects.

Ideal Candidate:

- The ideal candidate is having strong understanding of cybersecurity risk management in large enterprise environment. Having spent time managing audits and ensuring cyber controls are in place and working effectively.

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

- 5-7 years of experience in operational technology (OT) and cybersecurity, preferably in manufacturing, industrial, or critical infrastructure environments.

- Strong knowledge of regulatory and standards requirements at regional and global levels (e.g., CMMC, EASA Part-IS, IA, and contractual cybersecurity obligations).

- Proven ability to lead projects and manage cybersecurity initiatives, coordinating cross-functional teams and driving actions to closure.

At Avio Aero, a GE Aerospace Business unit, we’ve been reimagining the power of flight for more than 100 years. We are specialized in the design, production and maintenance of components and systems for both the civil and military aviation.

As IT Product Owner for Supply Chain, you will lead the evolution and management of digital platforms and drive projects that enable the Avio Aero Supply Chain organization to meet the specific requirements and regulations of military programs, with a particular focus on manufacturing and quality processes.
In this role you will ensure alignment with civil program platforms, leveraging shared blueprints, infrastructures, and vendors to maximize efficiency.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

- Own the whole Digital application lifecycle, from requirements gathering to deployment, adoption, and maintenance.
- Manage project schedule, risks, costs, and any non-standard events ensuring successful delivery and measurable customer impact through KPIs.
- Act as a bridge between Business functions, IT, external stakeholders maintaining clear communication with end-users and management.
- Contribute to the Digital operations to ensure business continuity, efficiency, and ongoing improvement.
- Proactively explore alternate technologies and make informed choices based on experience and impact analysis.
- Lead cross-functional teams to deliver digital solutions that meet military program requirements while ensuring compliance with industry standards and regulations.

- Act as the primary point of contact between Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Digital Technology teams for MES-related initiatives and continuous improvement activities.
- Drive the adoption, enhancement, and operational support of MES solutions, ensuring alignment with business objectives and enterprise standards.
- Identify opportunities to improve shopfloor processes through MES capabilities, digital manufacturing technologies, and integration with enterprise systems.
- Develop and maintain deep functional expertise in MES and shopfloor digital processes, acting as a trusted advisor for Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality organizations.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or related discipline.
- Good knowledge of Supply Chain processes.
- Experience working with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), preferably DELMIA Apriso, or equivalent shopfloor digital solutions.
- Understanding of manufacturing processes and shopfloor operations within a complex industrial environment.

- Experience supporting manufacturing process transformation and digital adoption initiatives.

- Provide on-site and remote support as required.

As a Lead Embedded Software Engineer you will play a vital role in designing, developing, and testing embedded software, firmware, platforms and systems for our mission-critical technologies and products. You will work with a team of passionate and skilled engineers who share your vision of creating innovative and reliable embedded systems. - Propose novel solutions to technical challenges, generate cost and time estimates for future bids and programs, and utilize hardware/software to demonstrate capability against customer expectations.

- Extensive experience in Ada for embedded software design, development, and testing.
- Knowledge of scripting languages (Python, Perl, Tcl, etc.) and code management tools (Git, CVS, SVN, Perforce, etc.)
- Experience with network protocols with an understanding of Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking concepts, including Ethernet, Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) tagging where applicable. Familiarity with Neighbor Discovery (ND) in IPv6 is highly desirable.

Job Description Summary
Join our team as an Electronics Assembler, where you'll perform precision disassembly, reassembly, and testing of cutting-edge electronic products using advanced tools and equipment. You'll mentor teammates, troubleshoot using schematics, and ensure every product meets the highest quality standards while adhering to safety regulations. With 3-5 years of electronics assembly experience and certifications like IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, and IPC-7711, you'll play a vital role in driving innovation and excellence in manufacturing.

Job Description

About the Role

Join our team as an Electronics Assembler III where precision, soldering skill, and hands‑on electronics craftsmanship are essential. You will disassemble, reassemble, test, and troubleshoot complex power conversion and control products, ensuring they meet strict quality and safety standards. This role is central to delivering products that power aviation technologies.

Key Responsibilities

- Perform precision soldering and rework on printed circuit boards (PCBs) and electronic sub‑assemblies to IPC standards.

- Disassemble and reassemble chassis, sub‑assemblies, and components with minimal instruction while maintaining high quality.

- Set up and operate test equipment: digital/analog voltmeters, oscilloscopes, Hi‑Pot testers, and other diagnostic tools; interpret schematics to isolate and repair faults.

- Mentor and cross‑train teammates in assembly, soldering best practices, and troubleshooting techniques.

- Interpret engineering drawings and specifications; recommend process and quality improvements.

- Maintain organized workstations, calibration of tools, and strict adherence to safety procedures and SQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost).

Required Qualifications

- Hands‑on soldering experience (see specifics below).

- Certifications: IPC‑A‑610, J‑STD‑001, and IPC‑7711 (or ability to obtain).

- Experience: 3–5 years of electronics assembly and testing in a manufacturing environment.

- Proficiency using hand tools, gauges, schematics, and electronic test equipment.

- Strong dexterity, excellent hand‑eye coordination, and basic computer skills.

- High School Diploma or GED.

- This role may encounter high risk or hazardous operations and/or include working shifts beyond a standard workweek. As such, a requirement of the role is to be at least 18 years of age by the time of joining.

Preferred Soldering Skills and Experience

- Demonstrated ability in both through‑hole and surface‑mount soldering (SMT and THT), including component replacement and rework.

- Experience with soldering under microscope, using hot air rework stations, irons of varied wattages, and solder paste/flux handling.

- Familiarity with solder quality inspection per IPC‑A‑610 criteria and performing corrective rework per IPC‑7711.

- Ability to solder fine‑pitch ICs, connectors, and power components reliably and repeatably.

title: Pittsburgh On Wing Support Test Operation Site Leader
location: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States of America
description:
Job Description Summary
The Pittsburgh On Wing Support Test Operation Site Leader is responsible for the end-to-end leadership of the Pittsburgh Test Cell operation, ensuring safe, high-quality, and efficient delivery of engine test in support of our customers.

This role owns Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) performance for the site, will lead a multi-shift team, and drives continuous improvement to meet customer commitments. The Pittsburgh site is nearing final phases of construction and remodeling – this leader will have the opportunity to transition the site into operation and build a best in class team and organization.

The Pittsburgh On Wing Support Site Leader will be expected to lead the site consistent with our FLIGHT DECK operating system to meet immediate business objectives and engage in structured problem solving.

On Wing Support is a 24 / 7 / 365 operation across multiple global time zones. This role is expected to be willing and flexible, within reason, to accommodate and support the global network.

Job Description

Roles & Responsibilities:

- Maintain, grow, and actively promote a safe, open-reporting culture within the team, ensuring the engine test cell is established and operated with an uncompromising focus on Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost in that order. Demonstrate through actions and decisions the highest standards of integrity, operational discipline, and hazard awareness in a high-energy test environment.

- Respect for People – Lead transparently, foster an inclusive and engaged team environment, and build a test organization with the technical depth, operational mindset, and diverse perspectives needed to safely commission and operate the engine test cell. Develop team capability through coaching, training, and clear accountability.

- Customer Focus – Understand what matters most to internal and external customers in an on-wing support test operation, including responsiveness, technical accuracy, turnaround time, and confidence in test results. Prioritize the team’s work to maximize customer impact, measure performance through the customer lens, and use feedback to strengthen test execution and service delivery.

- Continuous Improvement – Establish a candid, humble, and transparent approach to problem solving and learning within the test operation, using lessons learned from commissioning, early operations, and daily execution to improve standards, eliminate waste, and drive reliability, repeatability, and flow through proactive kaizen.

- Fulfil the obligations of the Accountable Manager to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and any other applicable regulatory authorities, ensuring the test cell achieves and maintains the certifications, approvals, operating readiness, and procedural control required to support projected customer, product, and capability demand. Provide leadership and oversight within GE Aerospace’s Quality and Safety Management Systems throughout start-up and ongoing operations.

- Ensure the test site remains compliant with all applicable domestic and international laws, environmental requirements, permit conditions, industry regulations, financial controls, and tax obligations, including those associated with operating and maintaining an engine test facility.

- Ensure that all fundamentals of FLIGHT DECK are implemented across the full scope of the test cell operation, including start-up, daily management, standard work, action planning, problem solving, and operating cadences, and use FLIGHT DECK to run the operation and continuously improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance.

- Contribute to the Global OWS ‘One Global Team’ approach by sharing test-cell start-up learning, operational best practices, standards, and lessons learned across the network; adopting global standards where appropriate; and leading or participating in kaizen activity to improve engine test readiness and execution.

- Operationally lead the team using a KPI-based performance management approach to deliver safe, compliant, and efficient engine test activity, including commissioning milestones, operational readiness, test throughput, schedule adherence, first-pass yield, equipment uptime, and turnaround performance.

- Develop and deliver the site’s long-term strategy for the engine test operation while identifying future capability expansions, new product introduction needs, and test technology enhancements required to support evolving demand.

- Ensure the site has the necessary resources to deliver the strategic growth plan and sustain test operations, including workforce planning, hiring, training and certification, retention, organizational design, tooling, infrastructure, digital systems, and capital investment needed to safely commission, operate, and scale the test cell.

- Ensure the site is a responsible and proactive member of the local community, operating the test facility with appropriate environmental stewardship, professionalism, and engagement, while contributing positively within the surrounding area.

- Build and maintain productive relationships with relevant stakeholders – including customers, other OWS sites, the Global OWS team, ATMRO sites, GE Aerospace Product, Customer, Engineering, Quality, and Technical teams, regulatory authorities, and local industry partners – to ensure strong alignment on test readiness, operational performance, and future capability needs.

Required Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelors degree from an accredited college or university and 5+ years of experience in aviation assembly, test, maintenance, repair, and/or overhaul.

- 5+ years of people leadership experience required.

Desired Characteristics & Experience:

- Safety first and Respect for People mentality

- Experience and ability to execute FLIGHT DECK Fundamentals

- Talent development

- Data driven decision making

- Accountability and ownership

- Strong oral and written communication skills

- Strong interpersonal and leadership skills

- Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems

- Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects
