description:
Job Description Summary

Job Description

Summary:

The Power Generation Site Compliance Leader & Business Operations Leader is a dual-role position responsible for strengthening the compliance culture and managing compliance risk across the Vandalia and EPISCenter sites, while also driving operational excellence across the Power Generation business. This leader serves as the primary point of contact for site-level compliance matters, partnering closely with site leadership, Site HR, and the Electric Power & Propulsion Compliance Leader to promote a culture of integrity, ethical behavior, and proactive risk identification and mitigation.

In addition, this role drives end-to-end business operations excellence for the Power Generation business, enabling safe, high-quality, on-time, and cost-effective delivery across the Vandalia and EPISCenter sites. The leader will accelerate FLIGHT DECK, develop and sustain cross-site standard work, lead structured problem solving and special projects, standardize operating cadences and escalation forums, aggregate and analyze cross-site performance data, and provide functional leadership in support of MES implementation and business operations integration. This role will report to the Power Generation Operations leader, with dotted line reporting to the Business Unit Leader.

Responsibilities:

Compliance Leader:

- Serve as the on-site compliance expert, advising management and employees on compliance policies and best practices.

- Develop, implement, and monitor site-specific compliance programs, policies, and procedures (Site Compliance Risk Management, Annual Risk Assessment).

- Prepare for leader site visits and round tables.

- Maintain visual compliance across the site (e.g. posters, monthly compliance updates).

- Monitor and deliver compliance-related training programs to all site personnel and new employees.

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date metrics on compliance-related activities.

- Stay informed on GE Aerospace compliance policies and procedures; share and communicate to all site employees.

- Collaborate with GE Aerospace risk owners (e.g. EHS, Security, Quality)

- Serve as intake point for Open Reporting concerns.

Business Ops Leader:

- Standardize operating cadences and escalation forums

- Define and institutionalize cross-site cadences with clear inputs/outputs, owners, and decision logs.

- Lead daily/weekly operating rhythm, tiered meetings, KPI reviews, and standardized escalation paths across sites.

Job Description Summary
The AI Engineer is the senior individual contributor who owns the end-to-end build and productionization of AI enabled engineering capabilities across the business organizations of an aero engine and propulsion OEM. The role takes the reference architecture and patterns set by the AI Architect and turns them into robust, secure, scalable production services with great UX, multimodal, agentic LLM and other AI solutions, hardened against real engine engineering data and workflows across design, simulation, test, manufacturing, and sustainment. It embeds with the engineering teams of its assigned business, owns the build and release lifecycle for the capabilities it delivers, and stays hands on, architecting and building services and making pragmatic engineering tradeoffs rather than reviewing from a distance. Deep credibility in the
physics and engineering of the product, turbomachinery, aerodynamics, combustion, heat transfer, structures, and materials, and product mindset shaped by certified, safety critical hardware are core to the role.

Job Description

In this role, you will:

- Develop and own product build and release procedures and the end-to-end delivery of AI solutions, for a single release or multiple releases, working across the immediate team and other teams across the businesses.

- Productionize multimodal, agentic LLM and other AI solutions, applied to engine and propulsion engineering problems across design, analysis, test, manufacturing, and sustainment, as robust, secure, scalable systems with great UX; architect and build end to end services.

- Ground every capability in the realities of aero engine, propulsion, and turbomachinery engineering, integrating AI with CFD, FEA, thermal and structural analysis, engine and test data, model-based systems engineering, the digital thread, and PLM, so it augments how engines are designed, analyzed, tested, certified, and sustained.

- Lead others to find creative solutions within complex, interdependent engineering and production processes with technical variety, turbomachinery design, analysis, and test cycles, employing sophisticated operational / product management, manufacturing, and engineering techniques, drawing on multiple internal and external resources and questioning conflicting data to arrive at decisions.

- Take the reference architecture, patterns, and governance set by the AI Architect and deliver against them, keeping solutions compliant with data, security, and export control requirements (ITAR / export control, CMMC, RMF / ATO) across classified and unclassified environments.

- Own the model and agent delivery lifecycle in production: data pipelines, CI/CD, containerized deployment, model and agent serving, monitoring, and the build and release pipeline.

- Interpret internal and external business challenges and recommend best practices to improve products, processes, and services; use industry trends to inform the decision making process.

- Lead the delivery of projects with moderate to significant technical complexity and risk; present business and technical discipline solutions to senior leaders.

- Inform technical investment decisions, compute, model hosting, tooling, and build vs. buy, and the resourcing needed to deliver, working within program and project budgets.

- Communicate complex messages and negotiate internally and with external partners, vendors, and customers to adopt a point of view and influence peers to act.

- Act as an expert resource and best practice authority for the engineers embedded across the businesses, providing technical leadership, design review, and mentorship without direct management authority.

- Develop peer, cross functional, and cross business relationships to maximize best practice sharing and team effectiveness.

- Transition delivered capabilities to program ownership with documentation and trained users rather than leaving orphaned pilots.

- Share technical, procedural, and business knowledge with others, and support a continuous learning culture through learning content, presentations, and mentoring.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a STEM major

- Minimum of 10 years of overall engineering experience

- Production AI/ML systems and end to end service delivery experience required throughout.

- This role requires the successful candidate to maintain a US Government Security Clearance; prerequisite for a security clearance is U.S Citizenship. Preference is given to candidates who currently hold a US Government Security Clearance.

- Legal authorization to use in the U.S is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening

- Working fluency in the physics and engineering of aero engines and turbomachinery, aerodynamics, combustion, heat transfer, structures and rotordynamics, and materials, with the judgment to tell where a model is physically credible; hands on familiarity with CFD, FEA, and thermal/structural simulation, engine and rig test data, surrogate and physics informed modeling, model based systems engineering, the digital thread, and PLM.

- Strong software development in Python and at least one systems language (C++, Rust, Go, or Java), with solid API, version control, and testing practice.

- Strong DevSecOps and MLOps capability: cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP), Docker and Kubernetes, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, observability, and tooling such as MLflow or Kubeflow, with security applied across DevOps and MLOps.

- Applied production experience with LLM, retrieval augmented generation, and agentic frameworks, including multimodal AI, building robust, secure, scalable services with strong UX, and moving solutions from prototype to scaled production.

- Ability to architect and build end to end services and integrate them with the digital thread, PLM, and existing enterprise and simulation systems.

- Working knowledge of configuration choices and related cost implications, compute, model hosting, and build vs. buy, and experience with complex solution configurations.

- Experience delivering inside aerospace & defense or comparable regulated constraints: ITAR / export control, CMMC, RMF / ATO, and airgapped or impact level environments. Business Acumen

- Understands how the internal and external business model works, engine and propulsion programs, certification, and service / MRO, and uses that understanding to prioritize delivery.

- A product mindset for safety critical, certified hardware: comfort with verification and validation, certification evidence, reliability, and the long product and service lifecycle of an engine program.

- Able to articulate the value of what is most important to the business, applying presentation and storytelling concepts for cross functional teams.

Leadership

- Acts as an expert resource and technical thought leader for colleagues with less experience, providing design guidance and mentoring.

- Strong oral and written communication, with strong interpersonal and leadership skills and the ability to communicate and influence effectively across all organizational levels.

- Demonstrated ability to lead programs and projects, with established project management skills and the ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs.

- Demonstrated change management / acceleration capabilities.

- Ability to negotiate internally and with external partners, vendors, and customers.

Job Description Summary
Intergalactic now a part of Unison, a GE Aerospace Company, is a team of engineers, technologists, designers, mathematicians, and problem solvers committed to a singular idea: reviving the no-boundaries mentality in aerospace. We are a team of the nation’s best, regardless of where we live.

The Electrical Systems Engineer will serve as a technical leader for high‑reliability digital power conversion and electric drive systems, spanning architecture, detailed design, verification, and validation of Thermal Management Systems. This role focuses on developing and qualifying TMS control systems, advanced DC/DC conversion hardware and controls for aerospace applications, including high‑voltage power conversion, motor drive systems, and associated protection, monitoring, and control circuitry. The systems engineer will drive cross‑functional integration across systems, hardware, test, and manufacturing teams, ensuring safe, robust, and compliant solutions that meet customer requirements for safety, quality, delivery, and cost.

While providing Thermal Management Systems requirements support, collaborating with mechanical and systems engineering teams to ensure integrated electrical and thermal solutions for high‑reliability aerospace hardware is a paramount function to this position.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities:

- Own system‑level requirements flow‑down for digital power conversion hardware, decomposing customer and system requirements into clear, testable hardware and firmware requirements, and ensuring traceability throughout the design lifecycle.
- Document and communicate design decisions, analyses, and test outcomes through formal reports and technical reviews, ensuring traceability and a strong customer‑driven focus.
- Lead architecture and detailed design of digital power conversion, including DC/DC stages, gate drives, protection circuits, sensing chains, and control electronics, with emphasis on high‑voltage and high‑power aerospace applications.
- Plan and execute verification and validation of digital power conversion hardware and systems, including procedure authorship, lab setup, and execution of environmental, functional, and performance tests (e.g., DO160/MIL-STD-461/MIL-STD-704‑type conditions, thermal, vibration, electrical stress).

- Lead high‑voltage testing and qualification activities, including partial discharge (corona) tests and insulation tests at altitude and ground level, using results to drive design improvements and ensure long‑term reliability.
- Work with AI&T to develop and improve automated test benches and lab infrastructure for digital power testing, including scripting and automation where appropriate, and act as a champion for lab safety, structured test procedures, and safe operation at high voltage and high power.
- Provide technical guidance and mentorship to early career engineers and peers in power converter design, HV test, and system integration, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, structured problem solving, and respect for people
- Contribute to proposals, trade studies, and technology roadmaps for TMS control systems, digital power systems, including evaluation of new topologies, devices, and architectures.

- Advanced degree (M.S. or Ph.D.) in Electrical Engineering or related discipline with emphasis in power electronics, power conversion, or electric drives.
- Significant experience (e.g., 15+ years) in electrical engineering and electrical systems engineering with focus on power electronics, digital power conversion, and/or electric drive systems, and controls hardware for aerospace or similarly demanding applications.
- Proven experience leading the design, verification, and validation of power conversion hardware (DC/DC, AC/DC, DC/AC) and associated control electronics.

- Strong background in electrical systems engineering, requirements decomposition, and PCB/schematic design for power and control boards (gate drivers, sensors, DSP/control boards, HVDC filters, EMI filters), including DO160/MIL-STD-461/MIL-STD-704‑aware design practices and integration with system‑level requirements.

High-mix low-volume manufacturing automation capabilities applicable to diverse tasks without requiring bespoke hardware and software development.

description:
Job Description Summary
At Avio Aero, a GE Aerospace company, we invent the future of flight, lift people up, and bring them home safely. We are a world-leading provider specializing in the design, production, and maintenance of components and propulsion systems for both civil and military aviation. Respect for people is core to our culture and commitment to FLIGHT DECK, our proprietary lean operating model. We attract, develop, and retain industry-leading talent from all backgrounds and cultivate communities where people are respected and empowered to reach their fullest potential. For the people of GE Aerospace, their work isn't just a job. It's their passion and purpose. We work and win as one team, accountable to each other and our customers, and we are always finding a better way to climb higher together. We were meant to fly.

As SMS Risk Focal on Site you will be responsible for managing hazards within the assigned plant and serving as a key liaison among Compliance, Supply Chain, Product Quality, Operations, and SMS.
Working in close partnership with cross-functional teams, you will lead investigations and the hazard management process from a Safety Risk perspective, supporting teams in defining actions required to ensure residual risk acceptability in accordance with company procedures.
You will also coordinate mitigation activities, maintain hazard records and support the organization in strengthening its Safety Management System (SMS), safety culture, and compliance readiness. In addition, you will participate in operational rhythms to help identify threats, hazards, and potential risk consequences related to products, services, and systems.
This role reports directly to the Safety Risk Management Leader.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities:

- Manage and update the hazard log and SAT records with accuracy and discipline
- Support cross-functional collaboration to ensure effective hazard read-across across processes, products, and organizations
- Lead preliminary investigations engaging risk owners, by gathering data, facts, and supporting evidence
- Collect and review reports, inputs, and operational signals related to potential safety hazards

The CES Business Intelligence team is building the next generation of AI-powered solutions for commercial, contracts, and operations. This is a multi-faceted engineering role. You'll spend most of your time developing AI/ML products by training models, developing applications, and creating APIs. You'll also contribute to AI strategy and partner with executive stakeholders to align on requirements, success metrics, and business impact. We're looking for someone who's excited to expand their technical skillset in AI/ML and deliver advanced solutions that directly impact daily operations.

What you'll do: Design, build, deliver, and maintain AI/ML products including LLM-powered applications, forecasting models, anomaly detection systems, and intelligent agents. Own the full AI/ML lifecycle: requirements analysis, model design, training, evaluation, API development, deployment, and operational support. Convert complex operational datasets into scalable AI capabilities that enable real-time decision support.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities:

AI/ML Product Development

- Define, build, and evolve AI-powered software products that accelerate Commercial Engine Services operations—including LLM applications, machine learning models, and intelligent automation for supply chain optimization
- Create Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that package domain-specific AI capabilities for reuse across the enterprise.
- Package AI/ML models as robust, well-documented APIs that enable seamless integration into dashboards, applications, and operational workflows.
- Collaborate with BI team to embed AI features into existing applications that enable natural language queries, predictive insights, and intelligent recommendations directly within user-facing applications

Technical Leadership & Collaboration

- Provide hands-on AI/ML technical leadership for our modernization initiative, setting best practices for prompt engineering, model evaluation, experiment tracking, and responsible AI development
- Partner with executive stakeholders and BI leadership to understand business challenges and translate operational needs into AI/ML capabilities
- Ensure AI/ML models deploy reliably to AWS infrastructure with proper monitoring, logging, and performance optimization
- Translate requirements into a prioritized backlog of AI/ML products, driving delivery to required timelines, quality standards, and measurable business outcomes
- Collaborate with data platform teams to design data pipelines that feed AI/ML models to ensure data quality, freshness, and proper feature engineering from the Databricks medallion architecture

AI/ML Infrastructure & MLOps

- Establish MLOps practices including experiment tracking (MLflow, Weights & Biases), model versioning, automated evaluation pipelines, and A/B testing frameworks for continuous model improvement
- Drive world-class quality through rigorous SDLC practices: Lean/Agile/XP, CI/CD, automated testing, secure coding, scalability patterns, documentation-as-code, refactoring, and performance engineering
- Implement monitoring and observability for AI/ML systems to track model performance, data drift, prediction latency, and error rates; build automated alerting for model degradation
- Design vector database architectures and semantic search capabilities to power RAG applications; optimize retrieval strategies for accuracy and latency
- Build evaluation frameworks for LLM applications—measuring response quality, accuracy, relevance, and hallucination rates; establish automated testing for prompt templates and model outputs
- Ensure responsible AI practices including bias detection, explainability (SHAP, LIME), privacy-preserving techniques, and compliance with enterprise AI governance policies

Innovation & Strategy

- Drive the AI/ML roadmap for Commercial Engine Services BI team by identifying high-impact use cases, evaluating emerging AI technologies, and building proof-of-concepts that demonstrate business value
- Stay current on LLM advancements, ML frameworks, vector databases, and AI application patterns; bring practical innovations that improve decision speed and operational outcomes
- Engage domain experts to ensure successful transfer of complex operational knowledge into AI models and intelligent systems
- Establish reusable AI/ML components, templates, and reference architectures that accelerate future development and enable the BI team to leverage AI capabilities independently
- Communicate AI/ML concepts, tradeoffs, and results to non-technical stakeholders through clear documentation, executive presentations, and live demonstrations

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Engineering, or related field from an accredited college or university
- Minimum of 3 years of hands-on AI/ML engineering experience building and deploying machine learning models and/or AI-powered applications to production

Desired Characteristics

Technical Expertise

- Write production-quality code that meets standards and delivers intended functionality using the most appropriate technologies for the project (e.g., Python, Java, C#, TypeScript—based on system needs)
- Proven experience building data platforms and production LLM-powered applications; strong understanding of prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and vector databases
- Strong foundation in supervised/unsupervised learning, time-series forecasting, classification, and optimization
- Experience with MLflow, model registries, automated training pipelines, A/B testing frameworks, and model monitoring; strong DevOps collaboration skills
- Expertise in development platforms and services: AWS, Visual Studio, Databricks, GitHub, etc.
- Experience building REST APIs (FastAPI, Flask) for model serving; understanding of authentication, rate limiting, versioning, and API documentation

Domain & Business Acumen

- Experience building AI/ML solutions for supply chain, manufacturing, maintenance, or operations analytics is a strong plus
- Understands business metrics and can translate AI/ML capabilities into quantifiable business outcomes (cost savings, time reduction, forecast accuracy improvement)
- Skilled in breaking down ambiguous AI problems, writing clear problem statements, and estimating model development effort accurately
- Stays current on AI/ML industry trends (LLM advancements, new frameworks, emerging techniques); brings practical innovations backed by proof-of-concepts

Leadership & Collaboration

- Leads by example through delivering AI/ML products while mentoring team on AI integration, prompt engineering, and model usage
- Able to work through ambiguity and drive alignment between AI capabilities and business needs; communicates model limitations, confidence intervals, and uncertainty clearly to non-technical stakeholders
- Continuously measures solutions against user expectations while balancing competing priorities and maintaining build quality.

Personal Attributes

- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain complex AI/ML concepts simply and translate effectively between data scientists, software engineers, and business stakeholders
- Effective collaborator who works seamlessly with BI developers, platform engineers, and business stakeholders
- Business-minded approach that focuses on operational metrics, user needs, and business impact while designing AI solutions that solve real problems rather than technical exercises
- Persists to completion by driving AI/ML products through deployment, monitoring, and iteration while taking ownership of model performance and continuously improving accuracy

Collaborate with multidisciplinary team of engineers to help lead our thermal-structural FEA analysis activities for hypersonic propulsion hardware design, As a Senior Structural and Thermal Analysis Engineer, you will help lead thermal-structural finite element analysis (FEA) for hypersonic propulsion hardware, supporting both ground and flight applications. Based in Rockledge, FL (with an additional posting location in Bohemia, NY), you will work in a multidisciplinary team. Your analysis will guide the design of hypersonic components from proof-of-concept through manufacturing and test.

This role has meaningful autonomy and visibility. You will use your technical depth, engineering judgment, and communication skills to lead design reviews, translate analysis results into design decisions, and keep programs on track against technical, cost, and schedule goals.

Job Description

In this role you will:

- Lead thermal-structural analysis of prototype components and subsystems to support rapid development of hypersonic propulsion systems.
- Build and run thermal-structural ANSYS/FEA models, working with teammates to define appropriate boundary conditions and constraints. These give a detailed account of each component's thermal-structural response.
- Apply engineering principles to assess the integrity and thermal-structural performance of components and subsystems, and use the results to guide design.
- Perform lifetime/cycle, reliability, and elastic-plastic analyses as program needs require.
- Help the team develop thermal-structural systems from proof-of-concept to final manufacturable components, including the transition to manufacturing and testing.

- Document and communicate assumptions, inputs, and results to multidisciplinary teams for review.
- Lead design reviews and prepare technical reports and presentations for the team and, when needed, the customer.
- Mentor and coach team members in thermal-structural analysis methods.

The Ideal Candidate

You are an experienced thermal-structural analyst who is comfortable owning complex analysis and explaining it clearly. You have deep FEA expertise, especially in ANSYS. You also understand how analysis fits into the broader design, manufacturing, and test process.

You are analytical and a critical thinker. You challenge existing processes, prioritize well, and learn quickly. You work effectively in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary team across multiple sites, and you lead through clear communication, sound decisions, and collaboration.

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering from an accredited college or university.

GE Aerospace is seeking a T700/CT7 (Turboshaft) Depot Subject Matter Expert - Quality / Repair Engineering to provide technical leadership across depot maintenance activity for T700/CT7 engines and modules. In this role, you will help interpret maintenance directives, evaluate maintenance activity for compliance and completeness, support troubleshooting and repair decisions, and strengthen documentation, training, and process discipline. - Interpret and apply technical directives, manuals, drawings, wiring diagrams, schematic diagrams, and maintenance publications relevant to T700/CT7 depot operations.

- Support proper use of tooling, support equipment, preservation requirements, and handling practices where quality oversight is needed.

- Demonstrated experience in T700/CT7 engine maintenance, depot operations, or closely related turboshaft engine maintenance support.
- Ability to interpret technical manuals, drawings, wiring diagrams, schematic diagrams, and maintenance instructions.
- Strong troubleshooting capability and experience supporting technical evaluation of defects, maintenance findings, and repair decisions.
- Experience with engine or module inspection, assembly, disassembly, repair, and test activity as relevant to depot operations.

- Background in work instruction validation, maintenance evaluation, audit support, or inspection documentation review.
- Experience supporting military, depot, or sustainment programs with disciplined configuration and procedural control.
- Demonstrated ability to drive continuous improvement utilizing FLIGHT DECK or similar lean operating system, corrective action follow-through, and practical process standardization.
- Ability to work effectively across quality, engineering, operations, and customer-facing teams to solve technical issues.
- Experience coaching teams on documentation quality, process discipline, and repeatable execution.

description:
Job Description Summary
As a Test Systems Technical Lead, you will be responsible for the technical direction, definition, and delivery of test system solutions across Power Distribution and Controls programs. You will own the technical solution for your product/project area, ensuring that test systems meet Safety, Quality, customer, regulatory, and business requirements while supporting program Delivery and Cost objectives.

Working as part of an Integrated Product Development Team (IPDT), you will lead the full test systems lifecycle from initial requirements capture through design, implementation, verification, release, and in-service support. You will demonstrate strong technical leadership, collaborate closely with Program and Engineering Project Managers, and provide guidance, coaching, and mentoring to engineers in the test systems team.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

1. Test Systems Lifecycle Ownership

Own the technical solution for test systems in your product/project area, ensuring alignment to customer, regulatory, and internal requirements. Lead the full Test Systems life cycle from concept and requirements definition through design, implementation, verification, formal release, and in-service support. Execute requirements, design, implementation, and verification using sound engineering principles, adhering to business standards, procedures, and program requirements. Ensure test equipment solutions are suitable for qualification, EMC, system verification, and production support, in line with DO-160, MIL-STD-461 and similar standards.

2. Technical Leadership

Own the technical direction and accountability for test systems within your project to meet customer and derived requirements. Monitor and steer the technical solution, ensuring rigor in design and technical reviews for your test solution. Collaborate with the Designated Technical Authority (DTA) to ensure test system architectures and strategies are aligned to the overall product architecture. Engage SMEs and Chief Engineer’s Office as needed to resolve complex technical issues, de-risk solutions, and ensure compliance with internal design guidelines. Ensure adherence to project plans, company and industry standards, and appropriate application of DTC (Design to Cost) and DFM (Design for Manufacture) / DFT (Design for Test) principles for test solutions.

3. Budget / Schedule / Scope Support

Support the Control Account Manager (CAM) and EPM in delivering the technical solution to the agreed scope, schedule, and budget for your project. Protect against internal and external scope creep for the test system, identifying potential changes early and supporting mitigation. Clearly communicate technical expectations to the engineering team, including definition of done, entry/exit criteria, and required deliverables. Support work package planning (e.g., rolling wave planning, milestones, and estimates) and provide input to technical metrics to monitor progress and health of test activities. Provide timely technical inputs to program reviews, Toll Gates, forecast updates, and risk & opportunity reviews as requested by EPM/PM.

4. Cross-functional Collaboration and Customer Interface

Act as the engineering interface to Program Management on test systems topics, clearly articulating technical direction, risks, and decisions. Liaise and interface with Systems, Hardware, Software, Manufacturing, Sustaining, Quality, Supply Chain, and Lab Operations to ensure integrated and robust test solutions. Support Program Manager and EPM in customer and certification discussions related to test system capability, coverage, readiness, and evidence. Ensure alignment and coordination with Manufacturing Program Manager (Launch Leader) and production test stakeholders regarding test strategy, manufacturability, and transition to production test environments.

5. Governance, Documentation, and Compliance

Assure proper documentation of technical data generated for test systems in line with engineering policies, configuration control, and quality requirements. Ensure test system requirements, design artefacts, verification evidence, and configuration baselines are defined, maintained, and traceable. Participate as presenter or reviewer in technical, design, and program reviews (including CEO/DTA reviews where applicable), ensuring issues, risks, and lessons learned are captured and addressed. Support change management activities for test systems, providing technical impact assessments for scope/schedule changes and feeding into program BCRs as required.

6. People Leadership, Coaching and Behaviours

Provide technical guidance and leadership to engineers and technicians working on test systems, ensuring clarity of priorities, deliverables, and standards. Coach, mentor, and train less experienced engineers, actively building technical capability and succession in the test systems community. Model and reinforce GE Leadership Behaviours – Act with Humility, Lead with Transparency, Deliver with Focus – and the supporting core values of Leading, Influencing, and Collaborating. Demonstrate and promote key team behaviours, including risk identification and mitigation, proactive information sharing, collaborative decision making, constructive feedback, problem solving, and driving Lean and cost out. Provide timely communications on significant technical issues or developments and use the defined escalation paths (Tech Lead/CAM → EPM → Subsection Manager/PMO → PM → senior leadership) where resolution is blocked or risks escalate.

Required Qualifications

Degree in Electrical, Electronic, or Software Engineering, or equivalent knowledge and experience. Significant experience in test system design, development, and integration, including hardware/software integration for complex systems, ideally in aviation or other high integrity/safety-critical environments. Demonstrated experience in qualification and EMC test equipment design, with working knowledge/awareness of DO-160, MIL-STD-461 or equivalent environmental and EMC standards.

Proven technical leadership experience delivering solutions to agreed scope, schedule, cost, and quality, preferably as a Technical Lead, CAM, or equivalent within a project environment. Strong problem-solving and solution-building skills, with the ability to break down complex problems, identify options, and drive to resolution.

Excellent communication skills, able to clearly convey complex technical topics to engineering teams, program management, customers, and leadership. Evidence of independent and sound technical judgement, including identifying when to escalate and when to seek DTA/CEO guidance.

Desired Characteristics

Demonstrable success in achieving and exceeding customer and program milestones for test system or product deliveries. Proven ability to deliver solutions on time, within budget, and to the required quality, operating effectively across TG3–TG9 project phases. Positive attitude, initiative, and proactiveness, with enthusiasm for continuous improvement, Lean thinking, and cost-out in test solutions. Experience mentoring and developing engineers, including delegating technical work, providing feedback, and supporting career development. Experience with aircraft power distribution systems verification laboratories or similar system integration/verification environments. Ability to gather support from multiple stakeholders and influence cross-functional teams, leveraging strong product and architecture understanding. Demonstrated collaboration across global, multi-function teams, creating environments where customer-centric creativity and outside-in thinking are encouraged.

Leadership Behaviours & Expectations

The Test Systems Technical Lead is expected to:

- Lead complex, cross-functional technical workstreams within programs, often spanning multiple products or platforms.
- Serve as the primary technical escalation point for test systems in their area, while using defined escalation paths for unresolved issues.
- Set high standards for safety, quality, and compliance, and actively drive continuous improvement in test strategies, methods, and tools.
- Act with humility, lead with transparency, and deliver with focus, always with unyielding integrity.

At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.

Job Description Summary

Job Description

À PROPOS DE GE AÉROSPATIAL :

Chez GE Aérospatial, nous faisons progresser les technologies aéronautiques d’aujourd’hui et de demain. Nous sommes l'un des principaux fournisseurs mondiaux de moteurs d'avion, de composantes et de systèmes intégrés pour les avions commerciaux et militaires. Spécifiquement, notre usine située à Bromont, se spécialise dans la fabrication des pièces des moteurs d’avion. Le site offre un environnement de travail dynamique alliant l’automatisation et la robotisation et une culture de gestion participative.

Ce que nous offrons :

- Un emploi étudiant adapté à votre calendrier de cours.
- Un horaire de travail entre 12 et 20 heures par semaine pouvant possiblement se transformer en 40 heures par semaine durant la période estivale.
- Travailler près de vos collègues afin d’avoir le soutien nécessaire tout en jouissant d’une bonne autonomie
- Prendre de l'expérience dans une entreprise offrants d’excellentes conditions qui est en croissance et offrant des possibilités d’embauche après vos études

RÉSUMÉ DU RÔLE :

Un poste de magasinier.ère en approvisionnement implique la gestion complète des stocks :

- Gérer la réception et le tri des marchandises pour assurer une organisation efficace.
- Stocker et organiser les produits en respectant les normes de sécurité et d'accessibilité.
- Préparer et expédier les commandes tout en respectant les délais et les exigences clients.
- Maintenir l'inventaire à jour en utilisant des outils informatiques de gestion.
- Collaborer avec les fournisseurs pour planifier et coordonner le réapprovisionnement.
- Utiliser et manipuler des engins de manutention tels que chariots élévateurs et transpalettes pour faciliter les opérations logistiques.

.

PROFIL IDÉAL :

Il est essentiel d'être rigoureux, organisé et de respecter les procédures de sécurité pour garantir la fluidité de la chaîne logistique.

QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES:

- Avoir 18 ans ou plus
- Être flexible pour travailler entre 12 et 20 heures par semaine, possibilité de 40 heure durant la période estivale.
- Posséder des habiletés mathématiques pour effectuer des calculs
- Être étudiant inscrit dans un programme d'études postsecondaires

QUALIFICATIONS SOUHAITÉES:

- Étudier dans un domaine connexe à l'approvisionnement ou à la logistique

Que nous fabriquions des composantes pour nos moteurs ou que nous innovions en matière de carburant et de réduction de bruit, nos équipes de GE Aérospatial sont dévouées et ont un impact mondial. Rejoignez-nous, voyez vos idées prendre leur envol et aidez à faire progresser l’industrie aérospatiale.
